risks.description: The screen serves a stale status (e.g. still 'open') after the exception has been resolved in the durable store, so the operator acts on a status the store no longer holds.
risks.basis: AC-UI-002 'the screen never shows a status the durable store does not hold'; fixture/app.py DEFECT=stale_read caches the first render.

risks.description: The exception detail screen fails to name the next action and/or who owns it, leaving the operator with nothing actionable.
risks.basis: AC-UI-001 'the exception detail screen names the next action and who owns it'.

risks.description: A request for an unknown exception id fabricates or defaults a status instead of returning not-found, showing a status the store does not hold.
risks.basis: AC-UI-002; fixture/app.py serves only EX-1 and returns 404 otherwise.

risks.description: Resolving the same exception more than once corrupts the durable status or owner, so a repeated operator action leaves the store inconsistent with what the screen shows.
risks.basis: AC-UI-002; the resolve endpoint mutates the durable store on each POST.

scenarios.title: Open exception screen names status, owner, and next action
scenarios.purpose: Confirm the exception detail screen an operator lands on states the status, why it was raised, who owns it, and the next action, matching the durable store.
scenarios.rationale: AC-UI-001 promises the screen names the next action and owner; this is the primary thing the unit adds.
scenarios.generating_risk: R2 — the screen could render without naming owner or next action, leaving the operator nothing to act on.
scenarios.isolation_note: Read-only: navigates and asserts text only, performs no mutation, so it cannot contaminate the next scenario.
expected_observations: next action: chase the carrier for proof of delivery

browser_steps.expect_text: next action: chase the carrier for proof of delivery

scenarios.title: Screen reflects resolved status after operator resolves (stale-render guard)
scenarios.purpose: After the operator clicks Resolve, the re-rendered screen must show the resolved status and closed next-action that the durable store now holds, never the pre-resolution status.
scenarios.rationale: This is the load-bearing AC-UI-002 check: a cached/stale render would keep showing 'open' while the store says 'resolved'.
scenarios.generating_risk: R1 — a stale render keeps serving the first status after resolution, so the screen and the durable store disagree.
scenarios.isolation_note: Mutates the durable store (resolves EX-1); final action restarts the ui service, which reseeds the store to the open EX-1, so the next scenario starts clean. isolation_key 'ui' prevents concurrent runs against the same store.
expected_observations: next action: none; the exception is closed

browser_steps.expect_text: next action: none; the exception is closed

scenarios.title: GET after resolve serves store status, not a cached one
scenarios.purpose: At the HTTP layer, GET / after a resolve POST must serve the resolved status the store holds, catching a stale render independent of browser rendering.
scenarios.rationale: AC-UI-002 must hold on the raw endpoint too; a browser-only check could miss a cache that only the rendered HTTP path exposes.
scenarios.generating_risk: R1 — the GET endpoint could keep returning the first-rendered status after the store moves to resolved.
scenarios.isolation_note: Mutates the durable store (resolves EX-1); final action restarts the ui service, which reseeds the store to the open EX-1. isolation_key 'ui' prevents concurrent runs.

scenarios.title: Resolving twice leaves the store consistent
scenarios.purpose: A repeated Resolve action must leave the durable status resolved and the owner unchanged, and the screen must reflect that single consistent status.
scenarios.rationale: Operators double-submit; AC-UI-002 requires the screen to always match the one status the store holds, even after a repeated resolve.
scenarios.generating_risk: R4 — a repeated resolve could corrupt the durable status or owner, desyncing screen and store.
scenarios.isolation_note: Mutates the durable store; final action restarts the ui service, which reseeds the store to the open EX-1. isolation_key 'ui' prevents concurrent runs.

scenarios.title: Unknown exception id returns not-found, no fabricated status
scenarios.purpose: Requesting an exception the store does not hold must return not-found rather than rendering a defaulted or fabricated status.
scenarios.rationale: AC-UI-002 forbids showing a status the store does not hold; a nonexistent id is the clearest way that invariant can be broken by falling back to a seed.
scenarios.generating_risk: R3 — an unknown id could fabricate/default a status instead of 404.
scenarios.isolation_note: Read-only GET of a nonexistent path; performs no mutation.

unresolved_questions: The fixture reseeds the durable store on every ui service start (main() unlinks and rewrites store.json), so persistence of a resolution across a restart cannot be verified — no acceptance criterion promises restart durability, so this was not scoped as a scenario. Confirm whether AC-UI-002 is intended to hold across service restarts.

AC-UI-001 requires the screen to state 'why the exception was raised' (reason), but no acceptance criterion explicitly names the reason field as mandatory beyond next-action/owner; the reason is asserted in S1 as part of the happy path but is not independently required. Confirm whether an absent/blank reason should fail the unit.

No requirement or approved command exists to simulate a missing/corrupt durable store from the operator's view; the app silently falls back to a seed. If AC-UI-002 should cover the store-unavailable case (screen must not show a status when the store cannot be read), a requirement and a way to induce that state are needed.
